content:
alex: hey team — quick heads up, I need to step away in ~25m for a hard stop. handing primary to @morgan. leaving checklist below, pls ack. :wave:

morgan: ack. I'm available for the next 2.5h. quick Q — any ongoing pagers or active mitigations?

alex: no active pager right now, but we saw a P1 earlier where KV-cache thrash caused higher tail latency on hosted generation. mitigation was applied (reduce batch size + enabled prefix cache). monitors look stable but p99 is still ~250ms above SLO in eu-west-1. leaving notes: runbook links, commands, and a short triage checklist. :memo:

riley: copying the runbook link for anyone who needs it: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash - includes rollback clip and warmstart flow.

alex: primary handoff checklist (short):
- escalate if any new pagers :rotating_light:
- if p99 > SLO for >15m, follow quick rollback (below)
- check incident-bot tags and set customer-impact if >50% customers degrade
- if models throttle, route to fallback model group (low-cost variant)

alex: quick rollback commands (kubectl snippet):
```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/redwood-runtime --to-revision=5
# then watch pods:
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -w
```

alex: warmstart KV cache helper (one-off):
```
# run on warmstart host
scp warmstart-seed.tar.gz infra@warmstart01:/var/tmp/
sudo systemctl restart kv-warmstart.service
```

morgan: got it. I'll set myself as primary in the incident-bot and post a quick status message every 30m while things are unstable. Incident-bot, please set oncall_primary=morgan now.

incident-bot: @morgan added as oncall_primary. Reminder: runbook link pinned. Auto-alerts to be routed to primary+secondary.

sam: quick note on customer impact assessment: if >10% latency increase vectors are read-only embeddings requests, mark impact as "degraded embeddings" and follow embeddings-sla runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/embeddings-degradation

jordan: if you need a temporary capacity bump, use the CLI to request burst (will auto-approve for oncall):
```
redwood capacity request --region eu-west-1 --gpu-pool inference-a --type burst --duration 30m
```

morgan: good to know. also adding a small triage checklist in thread for whoever picks this up next: 
- check alert history: /alerts?service=runtime
- verify metrics: tail latency, request rate, error rate (500s)
- check rolling deploys in last 2h (deploy bot channel)
- if deploy coincides, rollback to previous stable

riley: extra pointer: sometimes client retries amplify load. check ingress logs for retry loops (search for header x-rw-retry: yes). quick grep: `kubectl logs -n ingress ingress-proxy | grep x-rw-retry`

morgan: thanks. I'm going to annotate incident-bot with a short summary and set monitoring heartbeat checks to 1m. alex, have a good break — ping if you need anything before you go.

alex: thanks all. leaving one more note: if you escalate to SEV, follow customer notification template (in runbook). small snippet: 
> Customers may see delayed responses; we are investigating and will update every 30 minutes.

morgan: copy that. I'll take first 30m and then hand to @riley if I need to step out. everyone react with :eyes: if you read the handoff.

sam: :eyes:

jordan: :eyes:

riley: :eyes:

incident-bot: handoff acknowledged at 1764509150, oncall_primary=morgan, oncall_secondary=riley, notes pinned.

morgan: thread-check complete. leaving this thread as the single source-of-truth for the next 90 minutes. updating status in ops-dashboard and adding a link to the KB.
